meta.title: CMSG — Computational Materials Science Group
meta.description: The Computational Materials Science Group at Soochow University studies materials with physics-based simulation, data, and machine learning.

hero.badge: Computational Materials Science Group · Soochow University
hero.summary: From fundamental physics to emergent matter: understanding how structure, stability, and function arise, and using physics-informed computation to discover and design new materials.

intro.label: The Laboratory
intro.title: CMSG brings physics, data, and materials design into one unified working practice.
intro.body: Based in the School of Energy and the Soochow Institute of Energy and Materials Innovations (SIEMIS) at Soochow University, we develop computational methodologies, interatomic potentials, and open-source tools to tackle complex materials problems with clarity and precision.

research.label: Research Thrusts
research.title: Pioneering research pillars bridging atomic physics and macroscopic function.
research.subtitle: We tackle challenging problems in energy materials and condensed matter physics using first-principles calculations and AI.

items.title: Materials inverse design
items.summary: Starting from target macroscopic properties, we search for suitable candidates across the vast multidimensional space defined by element types, chemical stoichiometries, and crystal structures.

items.title: Physical discovery & interpretable AI
items.summary: Investigating physical mechanisms behind macro material behavior—ranging from superhard structures to negative thermal expansion—uncovering interpretable, transferable physical descriptors.

items.title: Water & nanoconfined transport
items.summary: Understanding how nanoscale spatial confinement reshapes molecular interactions, dynamics, and transport, uncovering microscopic paths to control nanofluidic friction and water activation.

join_us.label: Prospective Researchers
join_us.title: Join Our Research Group
join_us.body: We welcome enthusiastic undergraduate interns, graduate students (Master & PhD), and postdoctoral researchers from physics, chemistry, materials science, mechanical engineering, computer science, and related fields.
join_us.highlight: We emphasize efficiency, independence, and scientific rigor in an inclusive and collaborative environment.
